en: During the amihan season, the Philippines experiences cool, dry northeast winds that bring clear skies and lower temperatures.
Dark, towering cumulonimbus clouds often form in the afternoon and bring heavy rain, lightning, and thunderstorms.
Clay soil feels sticky when wet and holds water very well, making it ideal for planting rice in paddies.
Pumice is a light, porous volcanic rock that contains so many trapped gas bubbles that it can float on water.
In the early morning, water vapor in the cool air condenses into liquid droplets called dew on grass blades.
Venus is the brightest planet in our solar system and is easily visible in the sky just before sunrise or after sunset.
The Orion constellation, featuring three aligned stars that form its belt, is clearly visible in the Philippine night sky during December.
The moon appears to change shape over a 29.5-day cycle because we see different sunlit portions of it from Earth.
Tropical cyclones in the Philippines, locally called bagyo, always spin counterclockwise due to the Coriolis effect in the Northern Hemisphere.
The limestone formations in Palawan contain fossilized shells and coral, proving these rocks formed from ancient ocean sediments.
The dark topsoil in forests contains humus, which is made of fully decomposed leaves and dead organisms that enrich the earth.
A storm surge is a dangerous natural hazard where strong typhoon winds push a massive wall of seawater onto coastal land.
